limits: One fixed actual static-FP8 layer and six fresh trials per arm; replay blocks and15 sequential samples are not independent trials.
Exploratory unadjusted bootstrap resamples whole trial estimates, never individual replay blocks.
Chronological same-graph before/after changes confound process, elapsed-time and workload history; no matched untuned process identifies tuning as their unique cause.
This retained/interleaved protocol differs from the prior separate-process natural-layer protocol. A vanished gap does not retroactively prove the old result was measurement noise.
Public cache source is resolved at capture and does not recur during replay. Same public-1 alone does not prove identical native or physical GPU launches.
Native/trace observations are separate instrumented processes and cannot establish the kernel identity of actual latency-worker graphs.
Snapshots and order/time correlations are descriptive and cannot establish clocks or order as a cause.
No explicit-policy, managed-store, full-model accuracy or serving-throughput claim.
A public-default subgroup is conditional on observed natural selection, with its actual n reported; no all-six default assumption.
Cross-arm contextual ratios compare fresh processes and different natural winners. They do not isolate cache lookup during graph replay.
Preserved coordinator staging errors are outside the timing-worker cohort only when they are not actual timing/observe worker results.
An absent current stable gap would not prove the earlier separate-process4% runtime regression was noise.
interpretation: The same retained pre-tuning graph slows after startup in both arms. This is a measured chronological process/window change; no matched untuned process establishes tuning as its unique cause.
Interleaved independent-capture default/default comparisons do not reproduce a stable4% slowdown. The changed protocol cannot retrospectively explain the earlier separate-process result.

V2 selects default in4/6 timing trials. Its conditional default winner/miss subgroup is near neutral with an exploratory interval crossing1; the other two explicit winners remain22%+ slower than default during graph replay.
The v2/v1 aggregate winner comparison includes a lower median and a regression, with exploratory cross-process uncertainty crossing1. No universal v2 superiority or serving speedup follows.

The existing profiler uses eager timing and synthesized dynamic activations, while this study measures captured serving graphs using actual activations. Finite profiler minima do not establish graph-optimal candidate choice.
Both separate observers chose explicit winners; matched default/default native64-byte descriptors, seven attributes and launch signatures corroborate those diagnostic processes only.
next_decision: Design one bounded measurement-objective qualification on this same actual layer: current unspecified-policy control versus explicit graph policy, with matching tuning/capture lookup identity and unchanged v1 persistence/numerical guards. Review protocol before launch; no production policy change or broader performance claim is justified yet.
